title: 1 Chronicles 5
paragraphs: ¹ Now the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel — he was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, so the genealogy does not list him first by birthright. ² Judah was the strongest of his brothers and a ruler came from him, but the birthright belonged to Joseph. ³ The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. ⁴ The sons of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son, ⁵ Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,

⁶ Beerah his son, whom Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria carried into exile — he was a chief of the Reubenites. ⁷ His kinsmen listed by families in their genealogical records: the chief was Jeiel, then Zechariah, ⁸ and Bela son of Azaz son of Shema son of Joel, who settled in Aroer as far as Nebo and Baal-meon. ⁹ Eastward they settled as far as the edge of the desert this side of the Euphrates River, because their herds had grown large in the land of Gilead. ¹⁰ In the days of Saul they made war on the Hagrites, who were defeated at their hands, and they settled in their tents throughout all the eastern region of Gilead.

¹¹ The children of Gad lived across from them in the land of Bashan, as far as Salcah. ¹² Joel was the chief, Shapham the second, then Jaanai and Shaphat in Bashan. ¹³ Their kinsmen of the house of their fathers: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Eber — seven. ¹⁴ These were the sons of Abihail son of Huri son of Jaroah son of Gilead son of Michael son of Jeshishai son of Jahdo son of Buz. ¹⁵ Ahi son of Abdiel son of Guni was the head of their father's house.

¹⁶ They lived in Gilead in Bashan, in its towns, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon within their borders. ¹⁷ All of these were registered by genealogy in the days of Jotham king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel. ¹⁸ The men of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were warriors — men who could handle a shield and sword, who could draw the bow, and who were trained for war. There were forty-four thousand seven hundred and sixty of them ready for battle. ¹⁹ They made war against the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab. ²⁰ They were helped against them, and the Hagrites and all who were with them were handed over to them, for they cried out to God in battle, and he answered their prayer because they trusted in him.

²¹ They captured their enemies' livestock — fifty thousand camels, two hundred and fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys — and a hundred thousand men. ²² For many fell dead because the war was God's. And they lived in their place until the exile.

²⁶ The God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria — that is, Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria — and he carried away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan, where they remain to this day.
